title: Espresso: Exploiting the Sparsity Property in Event Sensors with Spatiotemporal Ordering
problem: Event-based vision sensors generate sparse high-speed event streams, but efficient stream processing without destroying sparsity properties is architecturally challenging.
motivation: Event cameras capture rapid object motion with minimal data, but realizing computational advantages requires hardware that preserves sparsity during processing.
method: Espresso designs an FPGA-based architecture for event-based vision that efficiently processes spatiotemporal event streams while maintaining sparsity. Uses ordered data structures and specialized compute patterns to avoid materializing dense representations.
key_novelty: FPGA architecture for sparse event stream processing that preserves sparsity throughout computation.
contributions: Achieves throughput up to 5000 fps in real-world scenarios
Maintains sparse data representations during processing
limitations: Not discussed; scalability to complex vision algorithms and power consumption unclear.
primary_theme: Sparse event stream processing via FPGA
